title: Act IV, Scene I

teacherSummary.text: Gertrude tells Claudius that Hamlet, mad, killed Polonius. Claudius realizes it could have been him and resolves to ship Hamlet away at once, and to manage public opinion.

I read “Mad as the sea and wind, when both contend / Which is the mightier” slowly and put it in my own words: Gertrude tells Claudius that Hamlet is as mad as the sea and wind fighting over which is stronger. How does Gertrude describe Hamlet's state to Claudius? My answer: Gertrude protects Hamlet by insisting he is mad, not dangerous; the image also shows the turmoil she has seen, and Claudius decides to send him to England.
